newsitem.title: JAPAN: Bandai names new president after merger failure.
newsitem.headline: Bandai names new president after merger failure.

text.p: Japan's top toy maker Bandai Co Ltd formally announced on Thursday that its president will step down from his post next month after the firm abruptly called off planned merger with Sega Enterprises .
"I feel responsible for the troubles related to the merger caused both in the company as well as the outside," Bandai president Makoto Yamashina told a news conference.
Bandai said Takashi Mogi, currently president of three of Bandai's units, will become the company's new president.

Yamashina added, however, that his resignation, to be effective June 27, was not to take responsibility for the failure of the merger itself, which was "simply a business deal that did not come through".
While giving up the presidency which he held for 17 years, Yamashina, the son of Bandai's founder, will stay on with the company as chairman.
Yamashina said it would be decided next month whether he would retain an executive capacity as chairman.
Six directors and two auditors will also step down from their current posts, Bandai said.
"I would like to concentrate everyone's energy on carrying on with business," Mogi told the same news conference, adding that Bandai would continue to seek fresh business opportunities.

On Tuesday, just a day before Bandai and Sega were due to approve a merger contract, they announced they had called off the deal after strong opposition from mid-level Bandai managers. They said they would instead pursue a loose tie-up in product merchandising and development.
The bungled merger tarnished the credibility of Bandai's top management, who were unable to quell dissent within the company over the plan, and pushed down the company's shares.
Bandai shares extended their recent losses on the Tokyo bourse, dropping 100 yen to end at 2,570 yen.
Bandai, Japan's top toymaker, was founded in 1950 by Makoto Yamashina's father, Naoharu Yamashina, who is also due to step down from his position as an advisor to the firm in June.

Sega, maker of the Saturn 32-bit video-game player, and Bandai, which is known for its Power Rangers series and virtual pet toy "Tamagotchi", said in January that they would merge to create a global entertainment giant rivalling Walt Disney Co of the United States.
